sources.title: Producers Guild of America, Rules and Procedures for 2027 Awards Eligibility - Television Series and Specials (AWARDS.SERIES/SPECIALS, 07.20.26)
sources.said: During the development/pilot phase, the producer may conceive of the program’s concept or format and pitches the project to networks and/or distributors. … select the pilot’s writer(s) and conceives of, or helps to create, a series “bible.” … During the production phase, the producer may select key members of the creative team, approve all storylines and scripts, participate in all department meetings … supervise and approve the programming budget … contact with the Production Company, network, studio and/or distributor … supervise and approve all location scouting and the selection of both stage and production facilities as well as vendors … They may also select the director, principal cast and other members of the producing team … view the dailies as well as the director’s cut, participate in the approval of the final cut of each episode … offer general supervision of the day-to-day operations of the shooting company as well as all talent and crafts … particularly where a showrunner guides a successful series in its initial season(s), creating crucial templates for later seasons to follow. … During the post-production/delivery phase, the producer may serve as the primary point-of-contact for delivery requirement issues, including final cuts, release dates and standards and practices … select or approve the choice of post-production facilities and negotiate any deals for their use … provide ongoing consultation regarding the marketing of the program … they must demonstrate a significant and dedicated commitment of time and resources to the production of the series or special beyond and in addition to their duties as an executive/employee. … The PGA may take special notice of any Participant who hinders the production process through unwelcomed intrusion into aspects of the process outside … their appropriate responsibilities. Should the PGA determine that a Participant has engaged in such detrimental behavior, it may, at its discretion, choose to deny awards eligibility to that Participant. … A Participant may not withhold or misstate information material to the eligibility determination process or materially interfere with the PGA’s efforts to gather accurate and confidential information. … supervise or approve the use of sound materials (including music, effects, and ADR)

sources.title: Producing Credits for Episodic Television (Scripted) | Producers Guild - Producers Guild (PGA Code of Credits, as of 9/24/2024)
sources.said: A Producer in a creative producing role from ideation & pitch through all phases of production and/or responsible for packaging and selling the series to the network or studio. … A person responsible for the creation of the series, including its concept, format and characters. … The Line Producer (or “Produced By”) reports directly to the Executive Producer and has the primary responsibility for the budget and logistics of the scripted series production, from pre-production through delivery of each episode. … Showrunner (or Co-Showrunner) which has overall creative authority and management responsibility for the entire scripted series. … The Co-Executive Producer reports directly to the Executive Producer, from whom the Co-Executive Producer assumes direct supervisory responsibilities for above and below-the-line operations.

sources.title: Fiction Producing Lab - Film Independent
sources.said: Taking place during the course of two weeks in October, the Fiction Producing Lab culminates with a pitch session with established executives … Applicants must control the rights to the project with which they apply. … However, each application must demonstrate serious attention to the film’s budget and articulate the reasoning behind the budget level. … Through the Lab, Fellows develop strategies and action plans to bring their projects to fruition. … The Fiction Producing Lab helps further the careers of its Fellows by introducing them to film professionals who can advise them on both the craft and business of independent producing.

sources.title: ACE 35 CALL FOR APPLICATIONS (ACE Producers)
sources.said: Through pitching practice training and sessions on leadership and core values, the producers learn more about themselves and each other … During group sessions led by consultants, producers are encouraged to offer each other script advice and analyse financing plans and marketing materials. … Applications will primarily be evaluated on the producers’ track record and motivation, followed by the strength of the project and its co-production and collaborative potential. … Have a fiction feature film project in development which is designed to attract international finance and distribution … Interactive sessions exploring international financing opportunities and strategies through detailed analysis of producers’ finance plans, with input provided by high-grade professionals from across the industry. … Group sessions and walk & talk discussions provide insight into early development problems such as preparing intention notes, working with talents and maintaining good relationships with writers and directors.

sources.title: PRODUCING: Curriculum | AFI CONSERVATORY (First and Second Year course descriptions), read 2026-10-31
sources.said: The practical aspect of the class involves writing log lines, creating a writer’s list, reviewing and critiquing screenplays, and introducing the fellow to the basic skill of pitching. … The lectures will delve into learning how to pitch as a team, the evolving changes in pitching strategies, the importance of concept in a pitch, as well as creating visual materials to use in various pitching forums. … The instruction includes modules on securing intellectual property rights (i.e., books, articles, etc.), above-the-line talent deals (actors, director, producer, writers, etc.), financing structures, distribution models (both traditional and next-gen), and various in-class negotiation exercises. … The Portfolio is a requirement for graduation and should reflect the Fellow’s skill, taste and understanding of the market. … In individual meetings, the Producing Discipline Head will discuss the Fellow’s growth over the past year and provide constructive direction to succeed in second-year curriculum and their thesis projects, while also building a slate of projects to shape their futures as producers. … The course examines the question of how to choose and work with a writer and the creative collaboration that follows. … With the benefit of classroom instruction and individual meetings with Faculty, each Producing Fellow prepares a Producing Portfolio demonstrating his or her ability to identify and present material for at least two projects. … In a combination of individual and group sessions which strengthen storytelling and writing skills, Producers and Directors initiate and develop a compelling and viable story that they control. … Key areas that are explored include the basics of business affairs (ownership and copyright, rights agreements); talent and key crew agreements; learning how to raise film financing; examining financial streams from a global perspective, from crowdfunding to foreign pre-sales and equity; … By dissecting the rapidly changing landscape, learning both from the past and the present, Fellows will gain an understanding of how the industry’s business models have evolved and how the economic viability of a project is determined. … Expanding on Boot Camp fundamentals, Fellows will develop production-ready budgets and schedules; learn how to secure locations and navigate FilmLA; understand how to complete required paperwork, permits, contracts, and deliverables; and manage creative teams while protecting story and vision. … Topics will include budgeting and scheduling feature-length films, evaluating film incentives and how to choose a shooting location, understanding the ins-and-outs of working with unions, setting up an LLC and tax preparation, how to run payroll, and reading cost reports. … Fellows will be exposed to financing waterfalls and distribution profit participation statements to understand how money flows once a film is released and how a financier recoups their investment. … Fellows will develop foundational skills in television-specific budgeting and scheduling, production management, and coordination across departments for multi-episode storytelling. … Accepted Fellows produce a look book based around their pilots written for SCR 631 & 632 and preside over a table read, tone meeting and production meeting in a workshop environment intended to emulate the writers room experience. … Fellows will learn the strategies and tactics of a film’s release including positioning, creative assets, audience identification, marketing, publicity, and distribution. … The course also builds marketplace literacy, guiding Fellows to identify television buyers across broadcast, cable, and streaming platforms and understand the types of projects those buyers are seeking. … This course is dedicated to the fundamentals of film financing and distribution covering topics such as private equity, foreign sales, distribution windowing, film festivals and markets, and who the players are in these spaces. … Producers must understand the writing process and develop a facility in the arena of story to evolve a shared vocabulary with creative collaborators. … A Producer who doesn’t understand the Post process is less able to help manage the process. … It is the culmination of the AFI Conservatory experience and demonstrates the Producer’s ability to work independently, incorporate feedback, refine concepts and assemble a professional presentation. … Producing Fellows will read unproduced film and television treatments and scripts with considered analysis, verbally present and discuss critical insights in a group setting, and synthesize their feedback and in-class discussions into follow-up written notes. … One of the first and most important practical skills an effective producer must possess and cultivate is the ability to carefully read, thoughtfully consider, and constructively critique screenplays and related materials to further their creative development. … Fellows will learn to manage writers’ rooms, support showrunners, and balance story development with production feasibility. … This course unpacks the story and craft logic of scenes and sequences from contemporary feature films, shorts and TV in order to give filmmakers a wider vocabulary and set of tools to develop the voice and vision of stories and deepen their professional practice.

sources.title: RNCP42775 - Grade_Master - Production audiovisuelle (certificateur: Institut National de l'audiovisuel), état Active, France compétences, read 2026-10-31
sources.said: Présenter - “pitcher”- un projet audiovisuel, pour convaincre de potentiels partenaires (diffuseurs, coproducteurs, distributeurs, financeurs) de s'engager dans le projet … Croiser exigences créatives, ressources nécessaires, partenaires potentiels et publics visés afin d'évaluer la viabilité technique et financière du projet. … Définir sa stratégie de production et construire le dossier de production en rédigeant les différentes pièces qui le composent en vue de sa présentation aux partenaires potentiels. … Construire une stratégie de développement et de pérennisation de l'entreprise en développant un portefeuille de projets et en mettant à profit les outils de pilotage budgétaire pour assurer la viabilité et la rentabilité de l'activité. … Analyser un scénario en dégageant ses forces et ses faiblesses pour identifier les réécritures à initier et accompagner l'auteur dans les différentes phases du développement du projet … Lire un projet audiovisuel d'un point de vue artistique en mobilisant sa culture générale pour estimer sa singularité et son potentiel. … Sur la base de l’analyse des partis pris esthétique et technique et du dépouillement du scénario, établir un devis prévisionnel tenant compte des financements envisagés. … Solliciter les différents guichets de financement et /ou partenaires potentiels pour obtenir les moyens nécessaires. … Sur la base des coûts prévisionnels du projet, définir sa stratégie de production pour construire son plan de financement … Recruter les chefs de poste et les prestataires pour affiner avec eux les hypothèses de fabrication en prenant en compte l'impact écologique du projet afin de valider les coûts envisagés. … Sur la base du devis validé et des engagements pris avec les différents partenaires, planifier les étapes de fabrication du projet en collaboration avec les équipes de production, pour livrer le projet conformément aux attendus et dans les délais prévus. … Organiser la sortie d’une œuvre audiovisuelle et sa promotion, en lien avec les différents partenaires en vue d’assurer sa visibilité et de lui faire rencontrer son public. … Sur la base du/des public(s) cible(s) et du positionnement dans le paysage audiovisuel, définir les conditions juridiques et économiques d’exploitation de l'œuvre avec les ayants droit en vue de sa diffusion dans les différents circuits d’exploitation. … Assurer la direction et la supervision du travail des différentes équipes, en veillant au respect du droit du travail et des conventions qui régissent le secteur, pour mettre en œuvre le projet. … Communiquer à des fins de formation ou de transfert de connaissances, par oral et par écrit, en français et dans au moins une langue étrangère … Gérer des contextes professionnels ou d’études complexes, imprévisibles et qui nécessitent des approches stratégiques nouvelles … Respecter les principes d’éthique, de déontologie et de responsabilité sociale et environnementale … Prendre en compte la problématique du handicap et de l'accessibilité dans chacune de ses actions professionnelles … Définir et négocier avec les différents partenaires financiers le cadre et le périmètre de la collaboration afin de contractualiser dans l'intérêt du projet et le respect de la réglementation en vigueur … Mettre en œuvre un management responsable articulant obligations d’employeur, qualité de vie au travail et communication interne pour fédérer une équipe autour d'un projet commun. … Mettre en place des processus de travail permettant la bonne information des équipes, un climat d'écoute, pour prévenir les conflits, les VHSS et faciliter la réalisation du projet audiovisuel. … Définir et structurer l’organisation administrative, juridique et financière pour créer et gérer une entreprise de production en conformité avec le cadre juridique et réglementaire. … Définir la stratégie éditoriale et économique de l'entreprise de production et son positionnement dans le paysage audiovisuel pour s'assurer de la faisabilité du projet.

sources.title: Producers Program (MFA) | UCLA School of Theater, Film, and Television, read 2026-10-31
sources.said: In the spring quarter of their first year, students will pitch a slate of at least three projects to a panel of industry professionals. … Students also may take courses that take a comprehensive look into the independent film world, what it is like to be a showrunner for a television series, feature film marketing, how to develop television projects from IP, intellectual property and film festival strategies. … Having optioned a screenplay or teleplay at the end of their first year, students will further develop that project and design a financing strategy that is realistic in the contemporary marketplace. … Students also learn the basics of producing: from inception of an idea through development, procuring talent and financing to planning and executing a production to marketing and distribution of the final product. … A feature project consists of an optioned screenplay that the student will further develop with the screenwriter and a comprehensive strategy that discusses how to package, finance, budget, market and distribute the project. … In addition to Introduction to Producing series, students in their first year also take lecture and seminar courses dealing with a variety of topics, including feature film and television development, studio and network management, production planning/budgeting, entertainment law and business negotiations, international financing and distribution, film festival strategies and the new CMS Common Course taken by all MFA students in the school of Film, Television and Digital Media. … This way, producing students can meet their classmates from the other TFT programs and start building a professional network in the classroom. … The student assists the director in realizing their creative vision and manages physical production. … Producers have to be able to conceptualize and oversee the entire life cycle of a creative project, and the Producers Program’s curriculum reflects just that.

Performance of a major portion of the producing functions on the Motion Picture in a decision-making capacity. … The Produced By credit applies to individuals primarily responsible for the origination and/or management of a Motion Picture’s production and delivery. … This role involves personally making regular, continuous, and substantial decisions regarding creative, production, budgetary, and legal concerns in a constructive and responsible manner across the film’s four stages of production. … Director demonstrated that they personally made regular, continuous, and substantial decisions regarding production, budgetary, and legal concerns in a constructive and responsible manner. … a significant and dedicated commitment to production of the Motion Picture that goes beyond safeguarding the financing … To be eligible for the Producers Mark, the producer should always place what is best for the production above all other considerations. … The Panel may take special notice of any credited Produced By who hinders the filmmaking process through unwelcomed intrusion into aspects of the process outside their appropriate responsibilities or through the creation of an inhospitable work environment. … A Produced By seeking awards eligibility may not knowingly withhold or misstate information material to the certification process … the effectiveness (or ineffectiveness) of each Produced By’s contributions. … any specific or unique contributions made by a Produced By that had a significant impact on the production (i.e. cultural/qualitative contributions that shaped the film) … a Produced By’s efforts to promote respect, safety, diversity, equity, and inclusion within the hiring process and throughout the making of the film.

sources.said: Candidates must have a legal agreement in place through which they control the project (e.g. an option, attachment, or shopping agreement). … Recognizing the crucial role that independent producers play in finding, shaping, and championing original filmmaking voices, the Sundance Institute Producers Program supports both fiction and nonfiction producers at all stages of their feature-length projects and their careers. … Through a year-round continuum of support — including grants, labs, fellowships, networking events, funding, and educational resource opportunities — producers are given the opportunity to build community with fellow producers and industry members, hone creative skills, gain additional knowledge of the field, and develop strategies for pitching, producing, financing, and releasing their films. … The program is designed to hone emerging producers’ creative instincts and evolve their communication and problem-solving skills at all stages of their next feature film. … Candidates must possess a distinct cinematic vision. … Some things to think about while applying to any of our programs include your personal connection to the material, why you are passionate about this particular story, how you intend to realize the project creatively and logistically, and the impact you hope to have on audiences. … The program is designed to hone emerging producers’ creative instincts and evolve their communicating and problem-solving skills at all stages of their next feature-length fiction or documentary film project. … You will be asked to answer a series of seven essay questions that will allow us to better understand your point of view as a producer and also why you want to make the project you are applying with. … Candidates must exemplify intention to evolve their producing practice as a lead nonfiction producer beyond the project they are applying with. … While the specific criteria for participation differs across our various programs, we are seeking passionate, bold, risk-taking, and creatively rigorous artists for all of our initiatives. … The lab is designed, in part, to focus on your creative input and sources.said: By graduation, you’ll be ready to step into the industry as a creative producer, line producer, or production manager, with the skills to manage budgets, schedules, financing, and equity structures, tax credits, pre-sales and commercial exploitation. … The course is a 5-module, 3-term 180-credit MA, taught over one year in-person, and addresses all the core competences required
